h: David’s Song Seeks the Salvation Still Awaiting Completion

p: The haftarah read with this parshah is
אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כב, א)
the words of this song" (Shmuel II 22:1).
that Parshas Ha'azinu is called a song;
but there are other songs in the Prophets;
but it connects to this parshah,
הוּבָא פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י עֲרָכִין יג, ב
that all the songs are in the feminine,
for after them comes pain and subjugation;
and in the future, "a new shir,"
"And David My servant will be their prince forever,"
his time had not truly come,
And as the haftarah concludes (Shmuel II 22:51):
"He is a tower of salvations to His king,
and does kindness to His anointed,
to David and to his offspring forever";
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא רַק לְזַרְעוֹ וְכוּלֵּי
nevertheless it is only "to his offspring," etc.
"And he said: Hashem is my rock" (Shmuel II 22:2):
alluding to the rock of Miriam's well,
which alludes to the Oral Torah,
to be saved from the war of the evil inclination,
אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רב, א)
and this is the Oral Torah.
grows stronger and renews itself every day,
and were it not for HaKadosh Baruch Hu
And of this it is said:
"and my rescuer; my God, my Rock,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב)
along the lines of what it says (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2):
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu is the heart of Yisrael?
'The Rock of my heart and my portion is God,'" etc.
וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים צא, ב; ד)
"I will say of Hashem, my refuge and my fortress,
my God in Whom I trust," etc.,
"and under His wings you will take refuge," etc.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים עה, יא)
along the lines of what is said (Tehillim 75:11):
"The horns of the righteous will be exalted";
who were anointed from a horn,
regarding what is written in the Sifrei (Sifrei Devarim 313),
that is, those who sought to rob
and afterward from Yisrael in general.
"and from my enemies I am saved" (Shmuel II 22:4):
these are from the nations of the world
גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִים אִתּוֹ (מִשְׁלֵי טז, ז)
"'He makes even his enemies at peace with him' (Mishlei 16:7)
and this is "from the troops and from the bandits."
And this is the connection to this parshah
which is the season of our joy,
and the war of Gog and Magog;
and we will be redeemed immediately.
For Shabbos is preparation for the days of work,
for all the holiness of the festivals
that fall in the days of the week
is included in the Shabbos before it,
and as has been explained several times.
